subject: art-design

moments.title: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon
moments.body: Picasso completes Les Demoiselles d'Avignon, drawing on Iberian sculpture and African masks. The painting is shown to a small circle but not publicly exhibited until 1916.
moments.takeaway: Foundational works can circulate privately for years before public reception.

moments.title: Analytic and synthetic Cubism
moments.body: Working closely, the two artists develop fragmented, multi-viewpoint compositions, then introduce collage and synthetic Cubism with newspaper and oilcloth.
moments.takeaway: A movement was forged by two artists working in such close dialogue their canvases were sometimes hard to attribute.

moments.title: Guernica
moments.body: Picasso paints Guernica for the Spanish Pavilion at the Paris International Exposition, responding to the German bombing of the Basque town.
moments.takeaway: Modernist form became a vehicle for documentary political witness.

now.title: Cubism's legacy today
now.body: Cubist strategies appear across graphic design, animation and 3D modelling. Museum displays increasingly include Picasso's contemporary African and Iberian sources.
now.open_questions: How should museums display work that drew on cultural sources without credit?

reflection: What collaborators do together is harder to attribute than what a single artist makes alone.
